should: Add a credits system to our SaaS: users buy credits, each API call uses one, and I need a history page.
Our game stores coins in users.coins and support keeps asking why someone's balance is what it is. Can we get a proper transaction log?
Two purchases at the same time took a user's balance below zero. Fix the wallet so that can't happen.
We only have a balance column on the users table. Migrate it to a ledger without changing what users see.
I need a points table for our loyalty program where every change is recorded and a nightly job checks that the totals add up.
should_not: Verify the signature on our payment provider's webhook before we credit the order.
Customers who get a refund keep their credits. Make refunds take the credits back.
Set up double-entry accounting with a chart of accounts for our company's books.

tasks.prompt: This Express app on PostgreSQL has a users table and nothing for balances yet. Add a coins balance with a ledger. Offers credit coins by transaction id, and users spend coins on items from the server's price table.
checks: A migration creates a ledger table with a unique constraint on the kind and reference columns and a signed integer amount column.
Exactly one function in the code base contains an UPDATE of the balance column, and the credit and spend handlers both call it inside a transaction.
The posting function updates the balance only when the insert reported a new row.
The debit is a single UPDATE with a balance condition in its WHERE clause, or runs after SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, and the code checks the number of rows changed.
The project's test run includes a test that posts the same reference twice and asserts that the balance changed once, and it passes.
A reconciliation command exists and exits with a non-zero status when a balance is changed directly in the database.

tasks.prompt: Our PHP app on MySQL updates users.balance directly in six places. Move it to a ledger. Users must not see any change in their balance.
checks: A migration creates the ledger table referencing users.id and inserts one opening_balance entry per account with a non-zero balance, keyed by the account id.
Running the opening-balance statement a second time inserts no rows.
A search of the code for statements that write users.balance finds only the posting function.
No handler contains both a call to the posting function and a direct balance update for the same change.
The posting function treats MySQL error 1062 on the ledger insert as an already recorded event and returns without updating the balance.
The reconciliation query over users and ledger returns no rows after the test suite has run.

tasks.prompt: Support needs to add or remove points from an account. Add an admin action for it on top of our existing ledger.
checks: The adjustment is posted through the existing posting function with its own kind, not by a direct update of the balance.
The stored entry contains the staff member's identity taken from the session and the reason text.
Submitting the same adjustment request twice with the same request id creates one ledger row.
A request without a staff session, without a reason, or above the configured cap is refused with a 4xx status and creates no ledger row.
A manual debit larger than the account's balance is refused unless it names the entry it corrects.
